title: Sheafification preserves sections on a weakly contractible object
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $U$ be an affine object that is weakly contractible, meaning that every epimorphism of sheaves of sets on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is surjective on sections over $U$. For a sheaf $F$ on profinite sets, form the presheaf on the pro-etale basis by the left Kan extension along the profinite-point site functor $a$ and then sheafify. The canonical map from the left-Kan-extension value at $U$ to the sheafified value at $U$ is an isomorphism. This is natural in $F$ and in morphisms between weakly contractible affine objects, and for abelian-group or commutative-ring valued $F$ it preserves the induced operations.
